Thus he affirmed Tawhid al-Rububiyyah (oneness of Lordship), which includes His sole creation and the universality and effectiveness of His will, and Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah (oneness of worship), which includes loving Him and worshipping Him alone without partner, and the acknowledgment of servanthood, which includes neediness towards Him in every respect.

(Section)

In the Jami' of al-Tirmidhi and the Sahih of al-Hakim, from the hadith of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The supplication of Dhu'n-Nun, when he called while in the belly of the fish: ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been of the wrongdoers.﴾

No Muslim has ever supplicated with it for anything except that Allah responded to him." Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a sahih hadith.

Also in the Mustadrak of al-Hakim, from the hadith of Sa'd, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Shall I not inform you of something which, when a matter of great importance befalls a man among you and he supplicates with it, Allah relieves him of it? The supplication of Dhu'n-Nun."

Also in his Sahih, from him, that he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Shall I guide you to the Greatest Name of Allah? The supplication of Yunus." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, was it for Yunus alone?" He said: "Do you not hear His saying: ﴿So We answered him and delivered him from distress, and thus do We deliver the believers﴾ [al-Anbiya: 88]? Any Muslim who supplicates with it during his illness forty times, and then dies in that illness, will be given the reward of a martyr, and if he recovers, he will recover forgiven."

Ibn Mas'ud said: No prophet among the prophets was ever afflicted with distress except that he sought relief through glorification (tasbih).

Meaning: desiring what is with Us, and fearing Our punishment. The pronoun in His words ﴿Indeed they﴾ refers, according to the majority of exegetes, to the prophets mentioned in this surah.

Al-raghab and al-rahab: hoping for mercy, and fear of the Fire, in their case, all of them.

He (Ibn al-Qayyim) said in Tariq al-Hijratayn (The Path of the Two Migrations):

God, glorified be He, has praised the nearest of His servants to Him for their fear of Him. Concerning His prophets, after praising and commending them, He said: ﴿Indeed they used to hasten to good deeds and call upon Us with hope and fear﴾.

So al-raghab is hope and desire, and al-rahab is fear and dread. And He spoke of His angels, whom He has granted security from His punishment: ﴿They fear their Lord above them, and they do what they are commanded﴾ [al-Nahl: 50].

In the Sahih, the Prophet ﷺ is related to have said: "Indeed I am the most knowledgeable of you about God and the most fearful of Him," and in another wording: "I am the most fearful of you toward God and the most knowledgeable of you about what I should guard against." He ﷺ used to pray with a sound in his chest like the boiling of a cauldron, from weeping. God, the Exalted, has said: ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge fear God﴾ [Fatir: 28]. Thus, the more a servant knows God, the more fearful of Him he is.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "The fear of God is sufficient as knowledge." The lack of fear of God is only due to the lack of the servant's knowledge of Him. The people most knowing are the most fearful of God. Whoever knows God, his modesty before Him, his fear of Him, and his love for Him grow intense, and the more he knows, the more his modesty, fear and love increase. Fear is among the most exalted stations of the path. The fear of the elite is greater than the fear of the common people; they have greater need of it, it is more fitting for them, and it is more binding upon them.

The servant is either upright or deviating from uprightness. If he is deviating from uprightness, his fear is of punishment for his deviation, and faith is not sound without this fear. It arises from three matters:

The first: his knowledge of the transgression and its ugliness.

The second: belief in the threat, and that God has attached its punishment to disobedience.

The third: that he does not know—perhaps he will be prevented from repentance and will be barred from it after he commits the sin.

By these three matters his fear is complete, and according to their strength or weakness, the strength or weakness of his fear will be. What drives a person to sin is either his lack of knowledge of its ugliness, or his lack of knowledge of its evil consequence, or both together, but his reliance on repentance drives him to it—and this is the most common of the sins of the people of faith. When he knows the ugliness of the sin and knows its evil outcome, and fears that the door of repentance will not be opened for him, that he will be prevented from it and barred from it, his fear intensifies. This is before the sin; once he commits it, his fear is even greater.

In sum, whoever has firmly settled in his heart the remembrance of the Hereafter and its recompense, and the remembrance of sin and the threat against it, and does not feel secure that he will bring about sincere repentance, will be stirred in his heart by a fear that he cannot control and that does not leave him until he is saved.

As for one who is upright with God, his fear is with every breath he takes, knowing that God turns the hearts, and that no heart is except that it is between two fingers of the fingers of the Most Merciful, the Mighty and Majestic. If He wills to keep it firm, He keeps it firm, and if He wills to make it deviate, He makes it deviate, as was established from the Prophet ﷺ, and most of his oaths were: "No, by the One who turns the hearts, no, by the One who turns the hearts."

Some of the early generations said: "The heart is more changeable than a cooking pot when its boiling is at full force."

Some of them said: "The likeness of the heart in the speed of its turning is a feather thrown onto a desert land, which the winds turn over, back and front."

It suffices in this the words of God, the Exalted: ﴿And know that God comes between a man and his heart﴾ [al-Anfal: 24]. So what settledness is there for one in this state? And who is more deserving of fear than he? Rather, his fear is constant in every state, even if it is hidden from him by the dominance of another state over him. Fear is the core of his heart, but it is concealed by the dominance of something else. The existence of a thing is other than knowledge of it. The first fear is the fruit of knowledge of the promise and the threat; this fear is the fruit of knowledge of God's power, might and majesty, and that He is the Doer of what He wills, the One who moves the heart, turns it, and turns it as He wishes. There is no god but Him.

[Chapter: The Station of Desire (al-Raghba)]

Among the stations of: ﴿You alone do we worship, and You alone do we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5] is the station of desire (raghba).

God, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿They call upon Us with hope and fear﴾ [al-Anbiya: 90].

The difference between raghba and raja' (hope) is that raja' is longing (tama'), while raghba is seeking (talab). Thus raghba is the fruit of raja'. For when one hopes for something, he seeks it. Raghba arising from raja' is like fleeing from fear. Whoever hopes for something seeks it and desires it; whoever fears something flees from it.

The point is that the one who hopes is a seeker, and the one who fears is a fleer.

The author of al-Manazil said:

"Raghba is from raja' in reality, because raja' is a longing that requires realization, while raghba is a conduct upon realization."

That is, raghba is generated from raja', but raja' is a longing, while raghba is conduct and seeking.

His words "raja' is a longing that requires realization" mean: a longing for something absent, uncertain in its attainment, even if it is established in itself, like the servant's hope to enter Paradise. Paradise is certain without doubt; the doubt is only about his entering it, and whether he will meet his Lord with a deed that prevents him from it or not. Unlike raghba, which only exists after the realization of what one desires. So faith in raghba is stronger than in raja'.

Therefore he said: "raghba is conduct upon realization."

This is the meaning of his words, and there is something to be considered in it.

For raghba is also seeking something absent, about whose attainment one is in doubt. The believer desires Paradise, and he is not certain of entering it. So the correct distinction is that raja' is longing and raghba is seeking. When longing grows strong, it becomes seeking.

(Chapter: On the words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has already preceded from Us—they will be kept far away from it (Hell).﴾ Q. 21:101)

The hadiths have already been mentioned concerning the people of happiness being in one of the two handfuls, and their being written, with their names and their fathers' names, in the register of the blessed before they were created. In the Sahih of al-Hakim, from the hadith of al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said:

"When there was revealed: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾

the polytheists said: 'The angels, Jesus and Uzayr are worshipped besides Allah.'

He said: Then there was revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has already preceded from Us—they will be kept far away from it﴾."

This is a sound chain. 'Ali ibn al-Madini said: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us: Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from 'Asim, who said: Abu Razin informed me, from Abu Yahya, from Ibn Abbas, that he said:

"A verse about which people do not ask—'I do not know'—either they recognised it and so did not ask about it, or they were ignorant of it and so did not ask about it."

It was said to him: "And what is it?"

He said: When there was revealed: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you are to it bound to come﴾

this weighed heavily upon the Quraysh, or upon the people of Makkah, and they said: "He reviles our gods." Then Ibn al-Za'bari came and said: "What is the matter with you?" They said: "He reviles our gods." He said: "What did he say?" They said: "He said: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you are to it bound to come﴾."

He said: "Call him to me." When the Prophet ﷺ was summoned, he said: "O Muhammad, is this specific to our gods, or to everyone who is worshipped besides Allah?" He said: "No, rather to everyone who is worshipped besides Allah." Ibn al-Za'bari said: "You have been refuted, by the Lord of this House"—meaning the Ka'bah—"Do you not claim that the angels are righteous servants, and that Jesus is a righteous servant, and that Uzayr is a righteous servant? And these are the Banu Mulayh, who worship the angels; and these are the Christians, who worship Jesus; and these are the Jews, who worship Uzayr." He said: The people of Makkah clamoured, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has already preceded from Us—they will be kept far away from it. They will not hear its faintest sound﴾.

He said: And there was revealed: ﴿And when the son of Mary was cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it, shouting﴾. He said: That is the clamour.

This objection which Ibn al-Za'bari raised does not apply to the verse, for He, glorified is He, said "you and what you worship besides Allah," and did not say "and those whom you worship" with "mā" (for things without reason). So the angels, the Messiah and Uzayr are not included; it is for stones and the like that do not reason. Also, the sura is Meccan and the address in it is to the idol-worshippers, for He said "indeed you and what you worship"; the word "antum" (you) and the word "mā" (what) nullify his question, and he was an eloquent Arab who would not have been unaware of that. But his objection was made on the basis of analogy and general meaning, whose ruling is general by the generality of its cause: i.e., if being worshipped entails being fuel of Hell, then this very meaning exists in the angels, Uzayr and the Messiah. He was answered with the distinguishing factor, and that is in several respects.

First: the angels, the Messiah and Uzayr are among those for whom the best reward has preceded from Allah; they are blessed and did nothing that would entitle them to the Fire, so they are not punished for others' worship of them, nor for their enmity with them. Equating them with idols is more abhorrent than equating sale with usury, or carrion with slaughtered meat, and this is the way of the people of falsehood: they equate what the Law, reason and natural disposition have distinguished, and they distinguish what Allah and His Messenger have equated.

The second distinction: idols are stones, not accountable and not speaking. If they are cast into Hell as a humiliation to them and to their worshippers, there is no one in that who does not deserve punishment. This differs from the angels, the Messiah and Uzayr, who are living and speaking; if they were cast into the Fire, that would be pain and torment to them.

Third: whoever worshipped these, by his claim, did not in reality worship them, for they did not call people to worshipping them. Rather the polytheists worshipped the devils, and they imagined that the worship was directed to these. They worshipped, by their claim, one who claimed to be worshipped alongside Allah and to have a god with Him; Allah, glorified is He, has absolved His angels, the Messiah and Uzayr of that, and only the devils claimed it. They, by their own belief, hold that they would be pleased to be worshipped alongside Allah, and none is pleased with that except the devils. For this reason He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And on the day He gathers them all and says to the angels, "Did these worship you?" They will say, "Glory be to You! You are our Guardian, not them; rather they worshipped the jinn; most of them believed in them"﴾. And the Exalted said: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan?﴾ And the Exalted said: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Glory be to Him! Rather they are honoured servants who do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command. He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not intercede except for one whom He approves, and they are fearful out of awe of Him. And whoever among them says, "Indeed I am a god besides Him," that one We shall recompense with Hell; thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾. So none was worshipped besides Allah except Satan. These answers are drawn from His saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has already preceded from Us﴾.

Reflect upon the verse and you will find these answers shining through its words; and success is from Allah.

The purpose here is the mention of the best reward which Allah had decreed for the people of happiness before their existence.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us; Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi narrated to us; 'Urwah ibn Thabit al-Ansari narrated to us; al-Zuhri narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf: "'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf fell severely ill and lost consciousness; then he regained it and said: 'I was unconscious?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Two harsh men came to me and took hold of my hands and said: Come, we will bring you to the Mighty, the Trustworthy.' So they took me, and a man met them and said: 'Where are you taking him?' They said: 'We are bringing him to the Mighty, the Trustworthy.' He said: 'Leave him, for this one is among those for whom happiness has already preceded, and he is in his mother's womb.'"

Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Baghawi said: Dawud ibn Rashid narrated to us; Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Qurashi narrated to me, from 'Amir ibn Sa'd, who said: "Sa'd came back from a land of his, and found people gathered around a man. He looked and saw that he was reviling Talhah, al-Zubayr and 'Ali. He forbade him, but it only seemed to incite him further. Sa'd said: 'Woe to you! Do you want to revile people who are better than you? Either you desist or I will invoke a curse upon you.' He said: 'It is as if a prophet from among the prophets is threatening me.' So Sa'd went off, entered a house, performed ablution, entered the mosque, and then said: 'O Allah, if this man has reviled people for whom the best reward has already preceded from You, and his reviling them has angered You, then show me today a sign that will be a sign for the believers.'

[The narrator] said: A she-camel [bukhtiyyah] will come out from the house of the Banu so-and-so, nothing will turn it back until it reaches him, the people will scatter, and you will place him between its legs and it will trample him until he is flattened." He said: "Then I saw Sa'd being followed by people saying: 'May Allah answer you, O Abu Ishaq! May Allah answer you, O Abu Ishaq!'"

And the Exalted said: ﴿And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion—the creed of your father Abraham. He named you "the Muslims" before, and in this [Qur'an]﴾.

That is, Allah named you before the Qur'an and in the Qur'an; so the naming by the Truth, glorified is He, of them as Muslims preceded their Islam and their existence. And the Exalted said: ﴿And Our word has already preceded to Our servants, the messengers: indeed they will be the victorious, and indeed Our host will be the conquerors﴾. Ibn Abbas, in the narration of al-Walibi from him, regarding the words: ﴿And give good tidings to those who believe that for them is a sure precedence with their Lord﴾, said: "Happiness had preceded for them in the first reminder." This does not contradict the view of one who said it refers to the righteous deeds they sent forward, nor the view of one who said it refers to Muhammad ﷺ, for happiness had preceded for them from Allah in the first reminder, through their deeds at the hand of Muhammad ﷺ; it is a good that Allah advanced for them, then advanced them through His Messenger, then will advance them upon Him on the day of meeting Him. And the Exalted said: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that had preceded, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took﴾.

The predecessors differed about this prior Book. The majority of the exegetes among the predecessors and those after them said: had it not been a decree from Allah preceding for you, O people of Badr, in the Preserved Tablet, that the spoils are lawful to you, He would have punished you. Others said: had it not been a Book from Allah preceding that He does not punish anyone except after proof, He would have punished you. Others said: had it not been a Book from Allah preceding for the people of Badr that they are forgiven, even if they did what they pleased, He would have punished them. And others said, and it is the correct view: had it not been a Book from Allah preceding with all of this, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took. And Allah knows best.

Al-Sijill: the paper on which things are written; al-kitab: the written content itself; the lam here has the sense of ʿala (on), meaning: We shall roll up the heaven like the rolling of a scroll over what is written on its lines. Then he argued from the like to the like, saying: ﴿As We began the first creation, We shall repeat it﴾.

(Chapter: On the wisdom for which the children of Adam will be resurrected uncircumcised)

When God, glorified is He, who is the Truthful in promise, and whose promise is not broken, promised that He would return creation as He began them the first time, it was part of the truth of His promise that He would return them in the state in which He began them, with their limbs complete and perfect. God the Exalted said: ﴿On the day We shall roll up the heaven like the rolling of a scroll for the writings. As We began the first creation, We shall repeat it, a promise binding upon Us; indeed We are ever doing it﴾. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿As He originated you, so you will return﴾.

Also, circumcision was prescribed in this world to complete purity and to be free of urine. The people of Paradise do not urinate or defecate, so there is no impurity there that would touch the foreskin requiring precaution against it. And the foreskin does not prevent the pleasure of intercourse nor hinder it. This holds if their continuance in that state in which they are resurrected is established; otherwise, it does not follow from their being resurrected in that way that they must remain in that state in which they were resurrected. For they will be resurrected barefoot, naked and uncircumcised, then they will be clothed, and their creation will be extended and increased thereafter, as the creation of the people of Paradise and Hellfire is increased. Otherwise, at the time of their rising from the graves, they will be in the form in which they were in the world, with their attributes, shapes and conditions, and each servant will be resurrected upon what he died upon. Then God, glorified is He, will create them as He wills. As for whether that foreskin, which completed their creation, remains in the graves or disappears, both are possible, and it cannot be known except by a report, which must be accepted. And God, glorified and exalted is He, knows best.

Scholars have differed about the land mentioned here. Sa'id ibn Jubayr reported from Ibn 'Abbas that it is the land of Paradise, and this is the view of most of the commentators (mufassirun).

There is another view reported from Ibn 'Abbas, that it is the worldly land which Allah opened to the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), and this view is the correct one.

Its parallel is His saying, Exalted is He, in Surat al-Nur: ﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth, just as He made successors those before them﴾.

In the authentic collection (al-Sahih) it is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said:
"The earth was folded up for me, its easts and its wests, and the dominion of my community will reach what was folded up for me of it."

A group of commentators said: what is meant is the land of Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), which is among the lands that Allah bequeathed to His righteous servants, and the verse is not restricted to it.

Safwan ibn 'Amr said: I asked 'Amir ibn 'Abd Allah, Abu al-Yaman: "Is there a gathering place for the souls of the believers?"
He said: "The land which Allah, Exalted is He, mentions: ﴿And We have certainly written in the Zabur after the Reminder that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾"
He said: "It is the land to which the souls of the believers gather until the Resurrection."

And they said: It is the land which Allah bequeathes to the believers in this world.

(A subtle point)
Consider the words of the Messiah in this glad tidings: "Indeed, the kingdom of God will be taken from you and given to another nation." How you find it corresponds to His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We have certainly written in the Zabur after the Reminder that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾.

(Section: on mention of the second rank, which is the rank of writing)
What indicates this has already been mentioned at the beginning of the book from the texts of the Qur'an and the authentic, explicit Sunnah, so we mention here some of what we did not mention. He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And We have certainly written in the Zabur after the Reminder that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants (105). Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship (106)﴾

So the Zabur here refers to all the books sent down from heaven and is not restricted to the Zabur of Dawud (David). The Reminder is the Mother of the Book which is with Allah, the earth is the worldly earth, and His righteous servants are the community of Muhammad (may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him).

This is the most correct of the views on this verse, and it is one of the signs of the prophethood of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for he gave this news in Makkah while the people of the earth were all disbelievers, enemies to him and his companions, and the polytheists had expelled them from their homes and dwellings and scattered them to the far corners of the earth. So their Lord, blessed and exalted, informed them that He had written in the earlier Reminder that they would inherit the earth from the disbelievers, and then He wrote that in the books He sent down to His messengers.

The Book has been called the Reminder in the words of the Prophet (ﷺ) in the hadith agreed upon as authentic:
"Allah was, and there was nothing other than Him, and His Throne was upon the water, and He wrote in the Reminder everything."
This is the Reminder in which it was written that the world would become the possession of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). The revealed books have been called the Zubur (scriptures) in His saying: ﴿And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed, so ask the people of the Reminder if you do not know, with clear proofs and the Zubur﴾, meaning We sent them with clear signs and books in which there is guidance and light. The Reminder here refers to the two books sent down before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), namely the Torah and the Gospel. And the Reminder in His saying: ﴿And We sent down to you the Reminder so that you may make clear to the people what was sent down to them﴾ is the Qur'an. So in this verse is His knowledge of what was before it existed and His writing of it after His knowledge.

He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, We bring the dead to life and We write what they have put forth and their traces, and everything We have enumerated in a clear register﴾.

So He combined the two writings: the writing preceding their deeds before their existence, and the writing accompanying their deeds. He informed that He will give them life after He causes them to die, for the resurrection, and will recompense them for their deeds, and He alerted by His writing of them to this. He said "We write what they have put forth" of good or evil they did in their lives, "and their traces" what they established of a good or evil practice, so that others follow them in it after their death.

Ibn 'Abbas, in the narration of 'Ata', said: "their traces are what they left behind of good or evil", like His saying: ﴿On that Day man will be informed of what he sent ahead and left behind﴾.

If you say: this has been derived from His saying "what they have put forth," so what does His saying "their traces" add?

I say: it adds a great benefit, which is that He, glorified is He, writes what they did and what arose from their deeds, so what arises from them is as if they themselves did it, whether good or evil, and it is the trace of their deeds. So their traces are the traces of their deeds that arise from them. This view is more general than the view of Muqatil, and it seems Muqatil intended an illustration and clarification, following the custom of the early scholars in explaining a general term by one type or one instance of its referents, as an approximation and illustration, not as a restriction or comprehensive enclosure.

Anas and Ibn 'Abbas, in a narration of 'Ikrimah, said: "This verse was revealed concerning the Banu Salamah, who wished to move closer to the mosque, as their dwellings were far away. When it was revealed they said: 'Rather, we will remain where we are.'" Those who hold this view cite what is in Sahih al-Bukhari from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: "The Banu Salamah were in a part of Madinah, and they wished to relocate close to the mosque, so this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We bring the dead to life and We write what they have put forth and their traces﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O Banu Salamah, stay in your homes; your traces are being written.'" Muslim also related something similar in his Sahih from the hadith of Jabir and Anas. But there is consideration in this view, for Surat Ya-Sin is Makki, while the story of the Banu Salamah took place in Madinah. Unless it is said that this verse alone is Madani. Better than this is that it was recalled at this incident and pointed to it, and they were reminded by it there, either by the Prophet (ﷺ) or by Jibril; so this was called revelation. Perhaps this is what those who say in similar cases "it was revealed twice" intended. The point is that their steps to the mosques are among their traces which Allah records for them.

'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "If Allah, Glorified is He, were to leave anything of the son of Adam, He would leave what the winds have effaced of a trace."

Masruq said: "No man takes a step except that a good deed or a bad deed is recorded for him."

The point is that His saying: ﴿And everything We have enumerated in a clear register﴾, which is the Preserved Tablet, the Mother of the Book, and the Reminder in which everything is written, includes the writing of the deeds of the servants before they do them. Enumeration in the Book includes His knowledge of them, their preservation, encompassing their number, and recording them in it.

He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And there is no creature on earth nor bird that flies with its two wings but they are communities like you. We have not neglected in the Book anything. Then to their Lord they will be gathered﴾

There has been difference concerning the Book here: whether it is the Qur'an or the Preserved Tablet, on two views. One group said it means the Qur'an, and this is a general term intended as specific, meaning: We have not neglected in it anything they need to be mentioned and explained, like His saying: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things﴾. It is also possible that it is a general term intended in its generality, and that everything is mentioned in it, in summary and in detail, as Ibn Mas'ud said: "Allah has cursed the woman who connects hair and the one who has it connected. Why should I not curse one whom Allah has cursed in His Book?" A woman said: "I have read the Qur'an and I did not find it." He said: "If you had read it, you would have found it." He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed the one who connects and the one who has it connected.

Al-Shafi'i said: "No calamity has befallen any of the Muslims except that there is a path in the Book of Allah indicating it."

Another group said that the Book in the verse means the Preserved Tablet in which Allah wrote everything. This is one of two narrations from Ibn 'Abbas, and this view is more apparent in the verse, and the context indicates it, for He said: ﴿And there is no creature on earth nor bird that flies with its two wings but they are communities like you.﴾

This implies that they are communities like us in creation, provision, eating, and the first decree: that they were not created in vain, but are subjected and made to serve, their creation, term, provision, and what they will come to have been decreed. Then He mentioned their end and their destination after their passing, then said: "Then to their Lord they will be gathered." Thus He mentioned their beginning and their end, and placed between these two states His saying: ﴿We have not neglected in the Book anything.﴾

That is, all of them have been written, decreed, and enumerated before they came into existence. So it is not fitting here to mention the book of command and prohibition; rather it fits to mention the first Book.

For the one who supports the first view, he may answer this by saying that the mention of the Qur'an here is an information about its including the mention of that and informing of it. So "We have not neglected in it anything": rather We have informed you of everything that was and that which is to be, in summary and in detail. This is strengthened by another matter: that this mention follows His saying: ﴿And they say: "Why has no sign been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say: "Indeed, Allah is able to send down a sign, but most of them do not know."﴾

So He alerted them to the greatest of signs and the one most indicative of the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which is the Book that contains the explanation of everything, and in which We have not neglected anything. Then He alerted them that they are a community among the communities in the heavens and the earth. This includes the introduction of the existence of the Creator, the perfection of His power and knowledge, the vastness of His dominion, and the multitude of His hosts and the communities that none but He can count. This includes that there is no god but Him, and no lord besides Him, and that He is the Lord of the worlds. So this is evidence of His oneness and attributes of perfection from the aspect of His creation and decree, and the sending down of the Book in which He neglected nothing is evidence from the aspect of His command and speech. "When Allah had decreed the creation, He wrote in His Book, which is with Him above the Throne: 'My mercy has prevailed over My wrath.'"

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 21, verse 107:

The sounder of the two opinions regarding His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And We have not sent you, except as a mercy to the worlds﴾, is that it is general in its scope.

On this interpretation there are two aspects:

The first is that the generality of "the worlds" means that all of them have benefited from his message. As for his followers, they gained through it the honour of this world and the Hereafter.

As for his enemies, those who waged war against him, their being killed quickly and their death are better for them than their life, because their life only increases the severity of their punishment in the Abode of the Hereafter. Wretchedness has already been decreed for them, so hastening their death is better for them than prolonging their lives in disbelief.

As for those who had covenants with him, they lived in this world under his shade, his pact and his protection, and by that covenant they were less harmful than those who waged war against him.

As for the hypocrites, by outwardly displaying faith in him they secured the protection of their blood, their property and their families, the respect due to them, and the application to them of the rulings of the Muslims in matters of inheritance and otherwise.

As for the distant nations, God, glory be to Him, through his message lifted the general punishment from the people of the earth, so that all the worlds gained benefit from his message.

The second aspect is that he is a mercy to everyone. But the believers accepted this mercy and benefited from it in this world and the next, while the disbelievers rejected it; yet this does not take him out of being a mercy to them, though they did not accept it. It is like saying: "This is a medicine for this illness." If the patient does not use it, it does not cease to be a medicine for that illness.

(Benefit)

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Tirmidhi said: The questioning of the dead is specific to this Ummah, because previous nations had messengers who would come to them with the message; when they refused, the messengers would withdraw from them and they would be punished with torment. When God sent Muhammad (ﷺ) with mercy as a leader for creation, as He said, Exalted is He: ﴿And We have not sent you, except as a mercy to the worlds﴾,

He withheld punishment from them and granted the sword, so that whoever would enter the religion of Islam would enter out of awe of the sword, and then faith would take firm root in his heart. Thus they were given respite, and from here the matter of hypocrisy became apparent: they concealed disbelief and displayed faith, and so they were among the Muslims in concealment. When they died, God appointed for them the two questioners of the grave, so that they might extract their secret through questioning, and so that God might distinguish the wicked from the good. ﴿God makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter, and God leads astray the wrongdoers, and God does what He wills.﴾

Others disagreed on this, among them 'Abd al-Haqq al-Ishbili and al-Qurtubi, and they said: the questioning is for this Ummah and for others.

Others held back from a judgment on this, among them Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr, who said: In the hadith of Zayd ibn Thabit from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed this Ummah will be tested in their graves,"

and some narrate it as "will be questioned." On this wording it is possible that this Ummah was singled out for that, but this is a matter on which no certainty can be claimed.
